progress.text: · Placed PDFs are drawn through pdfcraft's patched hayro crates: calculator functions whose idiv divides by zero or overflows, chains of stitching functions a hundred thousand deep, and mesh shadings with points far off the page, ten thousand overlapping triangles or forty thousand patches no longer panic, overflow the stack, run for over a minute or use more than 2 GiB of memory. A page with a /UserUnit, and its trim, bleed and art boxes, are sized in points. No readiness percentage change.
· Text threads by hand: click a selected text frame's in or out port to load

· macOS Dock Quit uses the same unsaved-document prompts as window and menu Quit. Repeated requests keep the current answers; Cancel retains every tab and unsaved recovery checkpoint, and completed Save/Don't Save answers exit through the ordinary event loop. No readiness percentage change.

· Orderly native exit writes the latest recovery state after finalizing current quit approvals; incomplete or stale plans keep their documents, and Undo to the saved state clears stale recovery. Unavailable or failed recovery is reported. Cancelable macOS Dock Quit remains open (#544). No readiness percentage change.

· Recovered documents keep a checkpoint until saved, closed or reverted, including a second crash before autosave. Restarted document IDs and explicit recovery folders preserve other snapshots; failed republishing retains the original. No readiness percentage change.

· Book numbering and style updates prepare every chapter before saving. Only closed native chapters are changed; imported IDML remains a read-only style/PDF source. If a later disk write fails, the error names the completed chapters; the batch is not a whole-book transaction. No readiness percentage change.

· Desktop write callbacks and CLI raster exports use the atomic writer too; open readers retain the original bytes, while private Unix modes and symlink targets survive replacement. Permanent tests cover both actual callers. No readiness percentage change.

· Save As, library edits and book collection edits persist prospective values before changing live state; failed writes preserve the document and existing collections. Save a Copy rebases data-source paths for its destination without changing the open document. No readiness percentage change.

· The Pen tool continues an open path from either end point, as in InDesign: the cursor shows it over an end point, a click there carries on drawing that path, a drag first reshapes the end point's direction lines, and the other end closes it. Object › Paths › Reverse Path (path.reverse); path.setAnchor; path.appendAnchor and path.close take a subpath. No readiness percentage change.

· Editing type on a path: the Type tool clicks, drags and double-clicks along the curve (the character under the pointer, not one on the straightened line), a click on the letters themselves hits the frame, and the caret and highlight bend with the path. No readiness percentage change.

· Type on a path has start and end brackets, as in InDesign: selected path type shows them across the path, and dragging either with the Selection or Direct Selection tool moves where the text starts or ends (text past the end bracket is overset). type.pathOptions {end}; IDML reads and writes EndBracket. No readiness percentage change.

· Window close and application/menu Quit ask about unsaved documents; later Cancel keeps every tab open, including earlier Don't Save choices. Approvals are rechecked after edits. Cancelable macOS Dock Quit remains open (#544). No readiness percentage change.

· Each running app keeps recovery data in its own locked folder; current folder and lock ownership are checked before writes and cleanup. Failed isolation disables recovery with a warning instead of sharing document IDs. No readiness percentage change.

· Native engine saves and exports replace files atomically; failed writes retain the original, private staging preserves Unix permissions, and valid long filenames work. Desktop Services and CLI raster exports remain separate follow-ups. No readiness percentage change.

· Hyphenation Zone applies to the Single-line Composer only, as in InDesign. With the default Paragraph Composer, ragged text hyphenates where InDesign does (aper-natem), giving the same line breaks. No readiness percentage change.

· The Tools panel's Fill/Stroke keys work: D (default fill and stroke), X (fill or stroke in front), Shift+X (swap per object, tints included) and / (Apply None), as color. commands; swap and default are one undo step (object.swapFillStroke, object.defaultFillStroke); the Color panel follows the proxy's fill/stroke choice. No readiness percentage change.
· Underlines and strikethroughs are drawn as one bar per stretch of text on screen, as in PDF export: a bar per letter left faint seams between the letters. No readiness percentage change.
· Properties › Transform shows rotation, shear and X/Y scale, and Rotate 90° and Flip Horizontal/Vertical buttons, as InDesign's does. No readiness percentage change.

· Edit › Step and Repeat has its InDesign dialog: Repeat (Count, or Rows and Columns with Create as a grid), Offset (Vertical, Horizontal, in ruler units) and Preview, which shows the copies while the dialog is open; Cancel takes them away and OK makes them as one undo step. No readiness percentage change.
· Double-clicking the Fill or Stroke box in the Tools panel opens the Color Picker with the selection's colour, as in InDesign (it opened the Swatches panel). No readiness percentage change.
· The Effects panel shows the level its settings apply to ("Group: Color Dodge 100%") and, as in InDesign, Isolate Blending and Knockout Group for a selected group. No readiness percentage change.

· The Eyedropper samples a placed image: clicking the photo with text (or objects) selected fills them with the image's colour under the pointer, as an unnamed colour (color.sample), as in InDesign. Images on locked layers can be sampled. No readiness percentage change.
· Words in capitals hyphenate like capitalized words (FERRUM COM-MODI), as in InDesign; Hyphenate Capitalized Words off keeps them whole. No readiness percentage change.

· Corner Options keep curved sides curved and round every corner point, including where an arc meets a line (a Pathfinder quarter circle with rounded corners stayed a triangle). No readiness percentage change.

· story.replaceRange, story.setText, notes, footnotes, endnotes, type on a path and table cells read \r and \r\n as paragraph returns, as frame.create and text.insert already did. No readiness percentage change.

· The View menu follows InDesign's: proofing first, then zoom, Rotate Spread, Screen Mode, Display Performance, rulers, Extras, Grids & Guides and Structure; the view items that sat at the end of the Type menu moved there. No readiness percentage change.

· Properties gains InDesign's Pathfinder section (Add, Subtract, Intersect, Exclude Overlap, Minus Back) with several objects selected; section titles and icon buttons have accessible names. No readiness percentage change.
· transform.move {copy}, Edit › Duplicate and Step and Repeat return the copies' ids, so a script can go on with them. No readiness percentage change.
· object.fill and object.stroke refuse a swatch name the document doesn't have (it painted nothing) and suggest the name meant (Paper → [Paper]). No readiness percentage change.

(printing): file.printers and file.print use craft-libs/craft-print for CUPS and Windows. DesignCraft retains PDF export, page selection, spreads, marks and bleed; dry runs create no temporary PDF or print job. Windows selects matching or default driver paper and shrinks oversized sheets without enlarging smaller ones; queue duplex defaults are preserved. Headless tests exercise exported bytes, job settings, dry runs and refusals; shared native Windows CI passes, including paused-queue submission and cleanup. PostScript, production print controls and physical output validation remain open. No readiness percentage change.

(UI.4–UI.5): Panel tabs can move into other groups, split the dock, float, resize and return to their saved locations through shared docking transactions. Layouts persist in custom workspaces; UI and control commands share the same validated action path. Shared pane geometry and widget-state theme application retain all five palettes and local fonts. Split panes send keyboard input only to the focused canvas and scope contextual toolbar IDs per pane. No readiness percentage change.
